standards.name: MIRAGE (Minimum Information Required for A Glycomics Experiment)
standards.abstract: MIRAGE targets reporting for glycomics experiments — studies that identify and characterise glycans and glycoconjugates (free glycans, glycoproteins, glycolipids, array/interaction assays) using analytical modalities such as mass spectrometry, liquid chromatography, NMR, capillary electrophoresis and glycan/lectin microarrays. Maintained by the MIRAGE Commission under the Beilstein-Institut (with broad international academic participation), MIRAGE provides publication-focused reporting guidelines and templates to ensure sufficient metadata and data exchange formats so that glycomics results are interpretable, comparable and reusable. The project publishes modality-specific guidelines (sample preparation, MS, LC, CE, NMR, glycan- and lectin-microarray, glycoproteomics, etc.), offers templates and a guideline-builder, and recommends repositories and identifier services (e.g. GlyTouCan, GlycoPOST) — while deliberately avoiding prescribing laboratory SOPs or quality benchmarks.

classification.rationale: The source material is a set of prose reporting guidelines, checklists and recommendations (narrative descriptions of what to report and why) rather than a single tabular metadata schema or an ordered workflow. Content is presented as guidance and recommended items to include, with templates/web tools referenced — matching the 'principle' category.

principles.principle: State the minimum information required for a glycomics experiment in publications
principles.evidence: MIRAGE stands for “Minimum Information Required for A Glycomics Experiment”. Since 2011, the MIRAGE Commission is supported and – together with scientists from the University of Georgia – coordinated by the Beilstein-Institut.

principles.principle: Improve the quality of journal articles by providing guidelines for the important data and metadata that characterise experiments
principles.evidence: The aim is that MIRAGE will improve the quality of journal articles describing glycomics analyses by providing authors with guidelines on how to include the most important data and metadata that characterize their experiments.

principles.principle: Report detailed sample-origin and sample-preparation metadata (generation, purification, modification)
principles.evidence: The sample preparation guidelines are designed to include all aspects of sample generation, purification and modification from biological and/or synthetic material.

principles.principle: Provide modality-specific reporting guidance (MS, LC, NMR, CE, microarrays, etc.)
principles.evidence: The development of publication guidelines is the key task of the working group. Up to now, the group has developed guidelines for sample preparations, mass spectrometric analysis, glycan microarray analysis, liquid chromatography analysis, NMR glycan recognition and structures, and capillary electrophoresis analysis.

principles.principle: Keep some guidelines intentionally minimal and supply templates to make reporting practical
principles.evidence: Reporting Guidelines for Glycan Microarray Data have been developed, approved by both the MIRAGE Commission and the community and published in 2017. These guidelines were drafted to be intentionally minimal and apply only to information required for generating interpretable data from a glycan array experiment.

principles.principle: Provide author-facing tools and templates (guideline builder, checklists, completed examples) to help produce compliant reports
principles.evidence: This page aimes at assisting researchers and authors to select those reporting guidelines that are most suitaable for a comprehensive reporting of the mass spectrometry experimental conditions and results when identifiying glycans and glycoproteins. General Features This is a general file that includes the data stamp when the work has been finalized, the responsible person and its contact information, the paper in which the data are published in a journal as well as the date when the checklist has been completed.

principles.principle: Recommend use of community repositories, registries and nomenclature resources alongside guidelines (link data to appropriate databases and IDs)
principles.evidence: In order to promote these achievements, the MIRAGE Commission recommends the community to refer to these projects when glycan data are published and/or deposited.

principles.principle: Advocate standardized graphical/nomenclature conventions and interoperable identifiers (e.g., SNFG, GlyTouCan) to support cross-platform comparison
principles.evidence: Symbol Nomenclature for Graphical Representations of Glycans (SNFG) ... The most recent version of SNFG can be found at here. GlyTouCan is the international glycan structure repository, developed and maintained at the Department of Bioinformatics, Faculty of Engineering, Soka University, Japan ... GlyTouCan is a freely available, uncurated registry for glycan structures that assigns globally unique accession numbers to any glycan independent of the level of information provided by the experimental method used to identify the structure(s).

principles.principle: Encourage journals, databases and the community to adopt and promote the guidelines (outreach, exemplar publications, repository recommendations)
principles.evidence: Promotion with Journals • In general: Glycobiology, PLOS, Carbohydrate Res., Glycoconjugate J. Mol. Omics (TF, DK, FL, NP, JP)

principles.principle: Do not prescribe laboratory standard operating procedures or fixed quality-assessment benchmarks — focus on reporting content and metadata
principles.evidence: The philosophical basis for MIRAGE is very similar to that of MIAPE: “It has always been a matter of policy that the PSI should neither attempt to produce standard operating procedures specifying how particular techniques should be performed nor attempt to establish quality assessment benchmarks.

standards.name: MIRAGE Sample Preparation Guidelines
standards.abstract: This guideline covers sample preparation metadata for glycomics experiments, where the research objects are carbohydrates, polysaccharides, oligosaccharides or glycoconjugates derived from chemical synthesis, biological sources (cells, tissues, organisms) or purchased/commercial materials. The document (MIRAGE Sample Preparation Guidelines, Version 1.0, 18 February 2016, doi:10.3762/mirage.1) provides a checklist-style set of reporting requirements for describing sample origin, processing (isolation, modification, purification) and the designation of the defined final sample. It is published as part of the MIRAGE initiative to standardize minimum information for glycomics experiments and addresses what to report about starting materials, enzymatic and chemical treatments, purification methods, and sample naming/nomenclature.

classification.rationale: The source is organised as prose guidance and a checklist of reporting requirements (instructions of what to report), rather than a table of named data fields with concrete data types or a sequential workflow. Sections such as 'Sample Origin', 'Sample Processing' (with subsections), and 'Defined Sample' give reporting instructions and examples, matching the 'principle' category.

principles.principle: Define sample (scope of 'sample')
principles.evidence: Here “sample” is defined as any carbohydrate, polysaccharide, oligosaccharide or glycoconjugate that originates from any given starting material.

principles.principle: Describe how original starting material was generated or obtained
principles.evidence:
Describe how original starting sample material was generated or
where it was obtained. Descriptions may include but are not limited
to material produced in the laboratory (e.g. chemically synthesized),
acquired from natural sources (e.g. human tissues) or purchased from
a commercial manufacturer.

principles.principle: Report vendor/item information for commercial materials
principles.evidence: In the case of commercial material, provide vendor and applicable item information.

principles.principle: Document biologically derived material details
principles.evidence:
Biologically derived material includes recombinantly expressed
proteins, cells, etc. as well as whole organisms or tissues. For recombinantly produced material, the cell type (e.g. CHO, HEK,
NS0 etc.) and growth/harvest conditions should be specified. Any
modifications to cells that influence the characteristics of the starting
material (e.g. genetic manipulations) should also be stated.
For material isolated from tissues, the tissue type, treatments and/or
storage conditions should be reported. The species should also be
provided.

principles.principle: Document chemically derived material and synthesis details
principles.evidence:
Describe how material was generated. If samples were synthetically
derived, provide information detailing synthesis steps or specify
where the equivalent reaction protocol is available.

principles.principle: Define the type of starting material used
principles.evidence:
Define the type of starting material used or produced that contains
the oligosaccharide to be used/analysed in subsequent experiments.
These may include glycoprotein(s), proteoglycan, glycolipid, GPI-
anchored, free-oligosaccharides, sugar-nucleotides or synthetically
derived material but are not limited to these definitions.

principles.principle: Report sample processing categories: isolation, modification, purification
principles.evidence:
The sample processing is divided into 1) isolation, 2) modification and 3) purification
subcategories. Required information for each is described below.

principles.principle: Describe enzymatic treatments used during isolation/modification
principles.evidence:
Describe any enzymes used to for the purpose of oligosaccharide
removal (e.g. PNGase F) or for modification of the starting material
(e.g. trypsin protease). Specify where it was obtained (vendor) or for
enzymes produced in-house, describe expression and purification
procedure. Also state if sample material was treated in-solution or
immobilized (SDS-PAGE, PVDF etc.) as well as temperature,
duration, volume, enzyme concentration.

principles.principle: Describe chemical techniques for oligosaccharide release and reaction conditions
principles.evidence:
Define the technique for oligosaccharide release (hydrazinolysis, β-
elimination etc.) or other chemical modifications. Provide details of
reaction conditions (temperature, duration, volume and chemical
concentrations).

principles.principle: Document chemical modifications to isolated material
principles.evidence:
Describe any treatments made to the isolated material. Explain the
type of modification employed (e.g. hydrolysis, sample tagging
Chemical modifications (including fluorescent labels), isotopic labelling,
permethylation/peracetylation, etc.). Include source of materials,
description of kits used, reaction conditions and detailed workflow.

principles.principle: Document enzymatic modification parameters
principles.evidence:
Document enzyme concentration, supplier, biological source,
incubation time and temperature. If novel glycosidase was used,
provide information indicating the origin (i.e. species) of the
enzyme.

principles.principle: Specify purification steps and describe materials/methods
principles.evidence:
Specify all steps used to purify starting material after
isolation/modification steps. Examples of procedures include solid
phase extraction (SPE), liquid-liquid extraction or other
chromatographic methods. For each method describe the all
experimental materials (e.g. stationary phase) and methods (e.g. flow
rates, fractionation etc.).

principles.principle: Provide a designation/name for the final defined sample
principles.evidence:
Provide a designation for the final sample in accordance with conventional terminology.
Name or specify the type of sample material to be analysed or used
in other experiments.

standards.notes: Source: MIRAGE Sample Preparation Guidelines, Version 1.0, 18 February 2016, doi:10.3762/mirage.1. Extracted principles are direct reporting instructions from the guideline.

standards.name: MIRAGE Mass Spectrometric Analysis Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines specify what metadata should be reported for mass spectrometric analysis of glycans and related samples. The research object is mass spectrometric data (MS and MS^n) of glycans, acquired under laboratory conditions on a variety of instruments and ion sources (ESI, MALDI, ion traps, TOF, etc.). The recording modality is mass spectrometry data files and associated parameter files, instrument settings, and descriptive metadata. The document is the MIRAGE (Minimum Information Required for A Glycomics Experiment) MS guideline (Version 1.0, April 24, 2013), produced under the MIRAGE initiative (Beilstein-Institut) and based on the MIAPE-MS template. It addresses the problem of incomplete or inconsistent reporting of mass spectrometry experiments for glycomics by defining a structured list of descriptors to allow reproducibility and repository submission, covering global descriptors, control and analysis software, ion source parameters, post-source componentry (collision cells, TOF, ion traps), and related discriminating experimental parameters.

standards.name: MIRAGE Glycan Microarray Analysis Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover glycan microarray experiments in which a ‘Glycan Binding Sample’ (proteins, organisms or other molecules that recognise carbohydrates) is applied to an array of defined or undefined glycan probes printed on a solid surface and detected by fluorescence scanning and image analysis. The MIRAGE Glycan Microarray Analysis Guidelines (Version 1.0, 22 June 2016) were published by the MIRAGE consortium/Beilstein-Institut and specify minimal information required to generate interpretable glycan microarray data, including sample description, glycan library details, surface and printing parameters, detection and data-processing information, presentation of results, and interpretation. The package also includes a Supplementary Glycan Microarray Information Template to record these items for reporting and repository submission.

classification.rationale: The source includes a concrete 'Supplementary Glycan Microarray Information Template' (a tabular template listing named metadata fields to be reported) and example supplementary documents that populate that template. Because the source provides an explicit table-like template with discrete field names intended for metadata capture, it should be extracted as a MetadataTable.

Description_of_Sample.descr: Free-text description of the Glycan Binding Sample (name, references, public DB IDs, origin, source, propagation for organisms, purity for proteins, fusion constructs, labelling).

raw_full_info.source_quote: The Sample description should include an appropriate name, previous references, public database IDs (if available), its origin (synthetic, natural, or recombinant), and its source including vendor or method of preparation.

Sample_modifications.descr: Description of any sample modifications (e.g. chemical labelling, sources/reagents).

raw_full_info.source_quote: If sample is directly labelled, describe the method and reagents. Sample modifications (including sources) used for chemical labeling of the Sample, e.g. fluorescein, biotin, etc.

Assay_protocol.descr: Protocol used for the microarray binding analysis including sample concentration, composition of solutions, blocking, incubation times and temperatures, washing and secondary reagents; pre-complexing details if used.

raw_full_info.source_quote: The protocol used for microarray binding analysis of Sample should include Sample concentration. Describe the composition of solutions, time and temperature used for blocking (preventing non-specific binding) binding, and washing, as well as application of secondary reagent(s) required for the analyses.

Glycan_description_for_defined_glycans.descr: Structural description of each defined mono-/oligosaccharide (sequence, linkage, anomeric configuration) using appropriate nomenclature and, when possible, accession numbers (e.g. GlyTouCan).

raw_full_info.source_quote: For mono- and oligosaccharides, the structure of each glycan, i.e. the sequence, linkage and anomeric configuration of each Glycan description for defined monosaccharide should be indicated using an appropriate nomenclature, which may be textual or symbolic as in SNFG (doi: 10.1093/glycob/cwv091). When possible, accession numbers assigned by an authoritative informatics resource, such as the GlyTouCan glycan structure registry (https://glytoucan.org/) should be included.

Glycan_description_for_undefined_glycans.descr: Information for glycans that are purified/partially purified or otherwise structurally undefined (e.g. source fractionation, shotgun arrays).

raw_full_info.source_quote: Glycans and glycoconjugates can be structurally defined; alternatively they can be purified or partially purified where structures are unknown ("shotgun" glycan arrays)... The requirements for identifying and documenting glycan structure are beyond the scope of these guidelines.

raw_full_info.source_quote: Methods/references for functionalization or derivatization of glycans, including the structures of linkers should be described. Any effects on the glycan structure; i.e., reductive amination of reducing monosaccharide, should be indicated. The purity of each glycan derivative should be indicated.

Printing_conditions.descr: Environmental and solution conditions used for printing (temperature, humidity, carrier lipids, printing markers).

The glycan probes that may have inaccurate immobilization amounts, as indicated by our quality control experiments, are shaded in grey in Supplementary Table 4.

standards.name: MIRAGE Liquid Chromatography Analysis Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover reporting of liquid chromatography (LC) experiments used in glycomics and related analyses, where chromatographic separations (columns, mobile phases, run parameters) and associated detection (e.g. MS, UV) produce chromatographic traces and fraction collections. The MIRAGE LC Guidelines (Version 1.0, 1 March 2018; doi:10.3762/mirage.4) are published by the MIRAGE initiative to define minimum and recommended metadata to allow interpretation, reuse and reproducibility of LC experiments. The document specifies field-level descriptors for general experiment metadata, equipment and column details, mobile phase composition, run parameters, pre/post run processes, detection settings, fraction outputs, data annotation and specific treatments (e.g. exoglycosidase digestion), and refers to other MIRAGE guidelines (Sample Preparation, MS) where relevant.

standards.name: MIRAGE NMR Glycan Recognition Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover NMR experiments and data used to characterize binding between glycans and receptors (proteins, cells, synthetic glycan-binding molecules). The recording modality is nuclear magnetic resonance (1H, 13C, 15N and multi-dimensional experiments) and related processed data, figures and tables. Published as Version 1.0 (21 September 2020) under the MIRAGE initiative, the document provides a comprehensive checklist/table of items that should be reported in manuscripts or supplementary material to allow interpretation and reuse of glycan–receptor NMR binding data. It is maintained as community reporting guidance addressing what sample descriptors, spectrometer/experiment parameters, NMR-specific measured quantities and presentation/interpretation items should be included.

classification.rationale: The source is presented as a structured reporting table (Supplementary Table-style) listing named fields and, for many items, explicit formats or expected value patterns (e.g. enums and y/n flags). Although advisory in tone, the document gives field-like entries (e.g. 'Origin: Natural/synthetic/glycoprotein', 'Magnetic field/cryoprobe y/n', 'Indicate: 1D/2D/3D; Name: ...'), so it is best represented as a MetadataTable.

standards.name: MIRAGE NMR Glycan Structures Guidelines
standards.abstract: These guidelines cover reporting of NMR experiments and data used to characterize glycan composition, conformation and dynamics for natural and synthetic glycans. The recording modality is NMR spectroscopy (1H, 13C and multi-dimensional experiments) with reported outputs including chemical shifts, J-couplings, NOEs, relaxation times, RDCs/PCSs/PREs and processed spectra/figures. The document (MIRAGE Guidelines v1.0, 21 Sept 2020, doi:10.3762/mirage.6) is published under the MIRAGE initiative to provide a comprehensive checklist for authors to include NMR-relevant sample descriptions, spectrometer and experiment parameters, data processing details, NMR parameters and data presentation/interpretation in manuscripts or supplementary material.

classification.rationale: The source presents a checklist organized as a set of named reportable fields (e.g. 'Origin: Natural/synthetic/glycoprotein', 'Chemical Shift Reference', 'Indicate: 1D/2D/3D', explicit 'y/n' for many items). standards.name: MIRAGE Capillary Electrophoresis Analysis Guidelines
standards.abstract: This standard concerns glycomics/glycoproteomics analyses of released N‑glycans from biological samples (example: human plasma) analyzed by capillary electrophoresis with laser‑induced fluorescence (xCGE‑LIF), producing instrument data files (.ab1/.fsa) and derived electropherogram fingerprints. The source material is the MIRAGE (Minimum Information Required for A Glycomics Experiment) CE guidelines supplementary information published in Glycobiology (example files and reporting templates). It is a reporting guideline published by MIRAGE authors (Lageveen‑Kammeijer et al. and collaborators) to specify the minimum information and example reporting for capillary electrophoresis glycomics experiments, covering sample collection and preparation, reagents and protocols, equipment and run conditions, data files and software/normalization, and analysis level.

classification.rationale: The source is organized as numbered prose sections and filled reporting examples (a checklist-style reporting guideline describing what metadata to provide), not a formal fields/columns metadata table nor a procedural DAG. It lists sections and items to report (instructions/examples), so it is best classified as PRINCIPLE.

principles.evidence:
Samples were collected from five healthy volunteers (male, nonsmoking, same age: all 28 years old in

at biweekly and six months at monthly intervals. Additional samples were taken within the time span of

consumption (data collected for the period two days before sampling).

principles.principle: Glycan release protocol (enzymes, volumes, conditions)
principles.evidence:
N-glycans were released from the plasma proteins as described previously (Ruhaak, L.R., Hennig, R., et al.
2010), with some slight modifications. Briefly, a total of 2 µL of plasma was mixed with 4 µL 2% SDS
(w/v; 2 % sodium dodecyl sulfate (≥99%, A2572, AppliChem) and 98% PBS (phosphate buffered saline;
aq 10× concentrated, BioReagent, P5493-1L, Sigma-Aldrich) and incubated for 10 min at 60 °C in a 96-well
polypropylene microplates (651201, Greiner Bio-One. After incubation, the remaining SDS was neutralized
with the addition of 4 μL 8% IGEPAL (v/v; 8% IGEPAL for molecular biology, I8896, Sigma-Aldrich with
92% PBS ). Subsequently, the N-glycans were released by adding 0.5 units of PNGase F (Peptide N-
q glycosidase F, BioReagent ≥95%, P7367, Sigma-Aldrich) in 1 μL PBS ,incubation was performed for 3 h at
37 °C.

principles.principle: Labeling reagents and labeling reaction conditions
principles.evidence:
A total of 2 μL of released N-glycans were labeled with 20 mM APTS (aminopyrene-1,3,6-trisulfonic
acid for fluorescence, ≥96.0%, 09341, Sigma-Aldrich) in 3.6 M citric acid (ACS grade for analysis,
1002440500, Merck-Millipore) and 2 μL 0.2 M 2-picoline-borane (≥95%, 654213, Sigma-Aldrich) in DMSO
(dimethylsulfoxide for HPLC, ≥99.7%, 34869, Sigma-Aldrich). The labeling reaction was stopped by adding
100 μL of 80% MeCN (v/v; 80% acetonitrile, LC-MS grade > 99.5%, 34967, Sigma-Aldrich with 20%
deionized water with R > 18.2 MΩ/cm (MQ) was produced by a Gradient A10 system from Merck-
Millipore).

principles.principle: Purification / cleanup method (HILIC-SPE) and conditions
principles.evidence:
The free APTS, reducing agent and other contaminants were removed by hydrophilic interaction
chromatography based solid phase extraction (HILIC-SPE) as described previously (Hennig, R., Rapp, E., et
al. 2015). Briefly, a 100 mg/mL Bio-Gel P10 (150-4144, Bio-Rad, Germany) suspension dissolved in a
MQ/ethanol (≥99.8%, T868.3, Carl Roth)/MeCN mixture (70:20:10%; v/v/v) was added to an AcroPrep™
96-well GHP Filter Plates (5030, Pall Corporation).

principles.principle: Elution and handling (shaking, incubation, collection)
principles.evidence: The labelled samples were loaded onto the filterplate, to improve glycan binding the plate was shaken at 500 rpm for 5 min using a Thermomixer. Subsequently, the wells were washed with 5 × 200 μL 80% MeCN with 100 mM triethylamine (≥99.5%, 471283, Sigma-Aldrich) which was adjusted to a pH of 8.5 using acetic acid (for luminescence, 45725, Sigma-Aldrich) and 3 × 200 μL MeCN. standards.name: MIRAGE Lectin Microarray Analysis Guidelines
standards.abstract: This standard addresses recording and reporting for lectin microarray experiments that measure glycan-binding profiles of glycan-containing samples (e.g., glycans, glycoproteins, cell lysates, cells, glycopeptides). The data modality is fluorescence-based microarray imaging and derived quantitative spot signals and heatmap/clustering outputs. The material is a template/checklist based on the MIRAGE guidelines (doi:10.3763/mirage.8) provided as a Supplementary Lectin Microarray Information Template and example methods; it is intended to ensure consistent reporting of sample description and preparation, lectin library composition, immobilization surface and array production, detection and image analysis, data processing/statistics, and data location. The source material is a MIRAGE-based supplementary template and example methods maintained by the MIRAGE community (reference: Tateno et al., J. Biol. Chem. 2011; doi:10.1074/jbcM111.231274) and accompanying Supplementary Documents.

classification.rationale: The source is a Supplementary Information 'template' and extracted tables that list named reporting fields (rows) each with their own concrete reporting slot (e.g., 'Immobilization surface', 'Manufacturer', 'Image analysis software'). The material therefore presents genuine field-level structure (a metadata table/template), not a prose checklist or ordered workflow.
